newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada, unions to resume talks.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada, unions to resume talks.

text.p: Armed by a strike manadate, unions at Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd will resume contract negotiations with the pulp and paper maker next week, a union official said Thursday.
Communications, Energy and Paperworkers union president Brian Payne said Thursday that talks with the company were scheduled to restart on July 4.
Payne said the unions expected the company to make concessions then. "I am expecting they are going to modify their position....I'm optimistic the employer will be prepared to make" changes, he said.
The 2,400 union workers at the company's three British Columbia pulp and paper mills voted earlier this week 96 percent in favor of a strike if necessary.
Talks collapsed June 16 over the company's demand for an eight-year contract, 365-day-a-year operation and greater workplace flexibility, the unions said then.
The unions must give 10 day notice before they can call a strike. Any decision to proceed with a strike will "depend on the flow" of negotiations and no timetable has been set, Payne said.
The union hopes to avoid a strike, he said. The workers have been without a contract since April 30.
Fletcher officials were not immediately available for comment. Fletcher is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd.
